po.title: Purchase orders
po.subtitle: Orders placed with suppliers. Approving a revision commits cost to the project.
po.createSubtitle: One order to a supplier. Issue it to commit the cost, or save it as a draft.
po.issueAwaitingApproval: This order was routed for approval. Once the approver acts, complete the issue to commit the cost.
po.draftRevisionBody: This revision is a draft. Issuing it supersedes the active revision and commits the new cost.
po.amendBody: Lines are pre-filled from the current active revision. Issuing the amended revision replaces the active one.
po.reasonRequired: A reason is required for a revision.
po.cancelBody: All open revisions will be cancelled.
po.cancelCommitmentWarning: Commitment ledger entries already written for this order will remain. Cancelling does not reverse them.
po.exceptionPendingNotice: A goods receipt against this order is awaiting exception resolution. No action is available on the order until it is dealt with.
po.totalIsPreview: The total is calculated here as a preview. The server recalculates each line amount when the order is saved.

lineError.materialRequired: Choose a material. Material lines cannot be free text.
lineError.quantityMustBePositive: Enter a quantity greater than zero.
lineError.priceMustBePositive: Enter a unit price greater than zero. The API does not accept a zero-priced line.

refusal.VENDOR_MAINTAINER_CANNOT_CREATE_PO_OR_PR: You maintain this supplier's record, so someone else must raise orders to them.
refusal.SYSTEM_ADMIN_CANNOT_APPROVE_BUSINESS_TRA: System administrators can't approve business transactions. Ask someone in the approval chain to act on this order.

grn.title: Goods receipts
grn.subtitle: Deliveries recorded against an active purchase order revision.
grn.createSubtitle: Record what arrived against an open order. A clean delivery is accepted and posted in one step; report a discrepancy only on the lines that need it.

receive.nothingBody: There are no open purchase orders. A delivery can be received once its order is confirmed.
receive.poSearch: Search by PO no. or supplier
receive.deliveryNoteHint: From the supplier's paper, if there is one.
receive.arrivedHint: Quantities are filled with what's still due. Change only what's different.
receive.reasonHint: What was wrong — damaged, wrong size, failed test.
receive.overReceived: {qty} more than still due. The full delivery is recorded; if it's beyond the allowed over-receipt, the receipt is flagged as an over-receipt.
receive.acceptedValue: Accepted value {amount} moves from ordered to received
receive.confirmOverReceipt: Some lines are more than still due. The full quantities are recorded, and the receipt is flagged as an over-receipt if any line is beyond the allowed over-receipt.

errors.rejectedOverDelivered: Rejected can't be more than delivered.
errors.purchaseOrder: Choose the order this delivery is for.
errors.nothingDelivered: Enter what arrived on at least one line.

sod.title: You raised this order, so someone else must receive it.
sod.body: Ask a colleague to receive the delivery, or request an exception if no one else is on site.
sod.pending: An exception was requested for this order. It can be received once it is approved.
sod.dialogBody: Explain why you need to receive this order yourself. An approver will review it.

grn.postBody: Posting moves the accepted value from committed to accrued in the commitment ledger. A posted receipt cannot be changed.
grn.cancelBody: A cancelled receipt cannot be reopened.
grn.postedNotice: This receipt is posted and can no longer be changed.
grn.overReceiptBody: More was delivered than ordered on at least one line, beyond the allowed over-receipt. The receipt is recorded in full and flagged on the order.
grn.exceptionBody: The delivered quantity exceeded what was ordered by more than the allowed tolerance, so this receipt was recorded but not posted.
grn.exceptionApprovable: As a supervisor you can approve this over-receipt, which returns the receipt to draft so it can be posted.
grn.exceptionNoPermission: Approving an over-receipt needs a supervisor. Until one approves it, the receipt stays held; it can only be cancelled from here.
grn.approveExceptionBody: This accepts that more was delivered than ordered and returns the receipt to draft so it can be posted. Only do this if the extra quantity is genuinely accepted.

lineError.receivedMustBePositive: Enter a received quantity greater than zero, or leave the line empty.
lineError.acceptedMustBePositive: The accepted quantity must be greater than zero. The API cannot record a fully rejected line (P6).
lineError.splitMustEqualReceived: Accepted plus rejected must equal the received quantity.

list.searchPlaceholder: Search by receipt number, PO or delivery note
list.emptyHint: Receive a delivery against a confirmed purchase order when goods arrive on site.

bills.title: Supplier bills
bills.subtitle: Bills received from suppliers, and how each one matches its purchase order.
bills.countLabel: {count, plural, =0 {No bills} one {# bill} other {# bills}}
bills.createSubtitle: For bills with no purchase order — utilities, rent, services and one-off purchases.
bills.nonPoOnlyNotice: A bill raised here cannot be attached to a purchase order. Use New PO bill for a bill against an order — it matches the order automatically on submit. This path is for genuine non-PO spend: utilities, rent, services and one-off purchases.

po.createSubtitle: For a bill against a purchase order. On submit it matches the order and the goods received automatically — no separate step.
po.chooseSupplierFirst: Choose the supplier first — the list shows that supplier's orders.
po.poNotBillable: This purchase order has no active revision to bill against. Approve a revision first.
po.linesInheritedHint: One line per order line — amounts prefilled from the order, edit to match the invoice.
po.noneTitle: No purchase orders to bill against
po.noneBody: A bill against an order needs an open purchase order with an approved (active) revision. There are none for this supplier yet.

bills.noProfilesTitle: No expense posting profile is configured
bills.noProfilesBody: A bill line has to name a posting profile that resolves to an expense or cost-of-sales account. None of the profiles in this organisation does. An administrator has to add one before a bill can be created.
bills.invoiceNumberHint: The supplier's own invoice number, as printed on their document.
bills.vatHint: Required. Enter 0 when the line carries no sales tax.
bills.expenseProfileHint: Determines the GL account debited when this bill is posted. Revenue profiles are not offered.
bills.netDiffers: Net {net} is {diff} {direction, select, more {more} other {less}} than {qty} × {price} ({computed}), as entered from the supplier's invoice.

lineError.description: Enter a description for this line.
lineError.quantity: Enter a quantity greater than zero.
lineError.unitPrice: Enter a unit price of zero or more.
lineError.net: Enter a net amount of zero or more.
lineError.vat: Enter a sales tax amount of zero or more. Enter 0 if there is none.
lineError.costTarget: Say where this cost belongs: a project with a BOQ item or a cost category, or mark it not chargeable to a project.

bills.submitBody: The bill can no longer be edited once submitted.
bills.approveBody: Approving clears the bill for posting. This cannot be undone from the UI.
bills.returnBody: The bill goes back to draft so it can be corrected and submitted again. Your reason is shown on the bill and kept in its history.
bills.rejectBody: A rejected bill stays on record and is never posted. Its supplier invoice number can be used again on a corrected bill. This can't be undone.
bills.postTitle: Post this bill to the general ledger?
bills.postBody: This writes the journal below. It can only be undone by a reversal.
bills.postUnbalanced: The lines do not sum to the bill total. Posting is blocked — this bill is internally inconsistent and should be raised with the backend engineer.
bills.postAccountProblem: The chart of accounts cannot answer which account is Accounts Payable, so the journal cannot be prepared.
bills.reverseBody: A reversing journal is written with the debits and credits swapped. Neither entry is removed. The reversal is refused if any payment has been allocated against this bill.

blockReason.not-draft: Only a draft bill can be submitted.
blockReason.not-submitted: The bill has to be submitted before it can be approved.
blockReason.not-approved: The bill has to be approved before it can be posted.
blockReason.not-posted: Only a posted bill can be reversed.
blockReason.already-reversed: This bill has already been reversed.
blockReason.unmatched: Three-way matching has to complete before this bill can be posted.

bills.emptyHint: Bills you record against suppliers will show up here.

create.title: New bill
create.intro: The number is assigned when you save. Submitting, approving and posting happen after saving, as separate commands.
create.kindPoDescription: Lines come from the purchase order and are matched to goods receipts.
create.kindDirectDescription: No purchase order — matching doesn't apply. You choose the expense profiles.
create.detailsDescription: Who sent the bill, and how they numbered it.
create.datesDescription: When the bill was issued and when it has to be paid.
create.invoiceNumberHint: As printed on the supplier's invoice.
create.duplicate: {number} is already recorded on {bill}. The server will not accept a second bill with this number from this supplier — check this isn't a duplicate.
create.projectHint: Rent, head-office supplies and other overhead belong to no project.
create.dueDateFromTerms: Set from the supplier's payment terms (Net {days}).
create.dueDateNoTerms: This supplier has no payment terms recorded. Enter the due date from the invoice.
create.linesPoDescription: One line per order line. Enter what this invoice bills.
create.linesDirectDescription: What the supplier is charging for, and where each cost posts.
create.choosePoFirst: Choose a purchase order to load its lines.
create.costLineNone: This project has no BOQ items or cost categories to charge to.
create.overReceived: Billing {qty} {unit} more than received on {grn} — the match will likely raise an exception.
create.overReceivedNothing: Billing {qty} {unit} and nothing has been received on this line yet — the match will likely raise an exception.
create.overOrdered: Billing {qty} {unit} more than ordered — the match will likely raise an exception.
create.totalsNote: A preview. The server calculates the totals it records from the lines.
create.netDiffers: Amount is {diff} {direction, select, more {more} other {less}} than {qty} × {price} ({computed}). The amount you typed is what posts.
create.failed: The bill could not be saved.
create.editIntro: Saving replaces the bill's details and lines. The bill stays a draft — submit it again from the bill when it is ready.
create.notDraft: Only a draft bill can be edited.

errors.purchaseOrder: Choose the purchase order this bill is against.
errors.project: Choose a project, or say the bill belongs to no project.
errors.costLine: Choose the BOQ item or cost category this project cost is for.

notice.postBlockedTitle: Posting is blocked by the purchase-order match
notice.postBlockedBody: The match result is {match}. Approve the exception or mark it disputed in Matching below before this bill can post.
notice.postFailedBody: The ledger did not accept this bill. Check that the accounting period is open, then retry.
notice.postingPendingBody: The ledger is writing this bill’s journal. This page updates when it finishes.
notice.reversedBody: A reversing journal cancelled this bill’s posting. The bill is read-only.
notice.returnedWhileEditing: Returned for correction — fix this before submitting again

journal.title: Journal items
journal.notYet: Journal items are created when this bill is posted.
journal.noAccess: This bill is posted to the general ledger. Viewing its journal lines needs the Manage journals permission.
journal.loadFailed: Could not load the journal entry.
journal.postedAs: Posted as <link>{number}</link>. Journal entries are immutable; corrections use a reversal.
journal.noAccessNumbered: Posted as {number}. Viewing its journal lines needs the Manage journals permission.

approvals.direct: Approved directly by {name} on {at} — no approval policy applied to this bill.

payments.title: Supplier payments
payments.subtitle: Money paid to suppliers, and how it settles against their bills.
payments.createSubtitle: Records a payment to a supplier, the bank account it was drawn on, and the bills it settles.
payments.accountingDateHint: The date this lands in the ledger. Defaults to the payment date.
payments.bankAccountHint: Only active accounts that allow payments are listed.
payments.amountError: Enter an amount greater than zero.

apply.title: Apply to bills
apply.hint: Tick a bill to settle it from this payment. Ticking prefills the full outstanding amount; edit it to pay part. Anything left over is kept as a supplier advance.
apply.enterAmountFirst: Enter the payment amount above to start applying it to bills.
apply.selectSupplierFirst: Choose a supplier to see its outstanding bills.
apply.none: This supplier has no posted bills with an outstanding balance. The whole payment will be recorded as a supplier advance.
apply.loadFailed: This supplier's bills could not be loaded, so bills cannot be applied here. The payment can still be recorded as an advance and settled later.

rowProblem.empty: Enter an amount to apply, or untick this bill.
rowProblem.not-positive: Enter an amount greater than zero, or untick this bill.
rowProblem.exceeds-bill: That is more than this bill still owes.

apply.exceedsAmount: The bills you have ticked add up to more than the payment amount. Reduce an amount or increase the payment.

payments.noBanksTitle: No bank account is available for payments
payments.noBanksBody: A payment has to name an active bank account that allows payments. None is configured. An administrator has to add one before a payment can be raised.
payments.approveBody: Approving clears the payment for release. There is no reject action over the API, so this cannot be undone from the UI.
payments.releaseBody: The bank account this payment draws on is under dual control: two authorised signatories must sign before it can be posted. Signing records your signature; the second signature releases the payment for posting. The approver cannot also release, and a signatory who approved a bill this payment settles cannot sign.
payments.releaseDualControlNote: This payment draws on a bank account under dual control (ADR-022). It must be released by two authorised signatories before it can be posted.
payments.releaseNotSignatory: You are not an authorised signatory of this payment's bank account, or signing would breach segregation of duties. Another signatory must release it.
payments.releaseAlreadySigned: You have already signed the release for this payment. A second, different signatory is needed.
payments.postTitle: Post this payment to the general ledger?
payments.postBody: This writes the journal below. It can only be undone by a reversal.
payments.postUnbalanced: The allocated and unallocated amounts do not sum to the payment total. Posting is blocked — this payment is internally inconsistent and should be raised with the backend engineer.
payments.postAccountProblem: The chart of accounts cannot answer which account is Accounts Payable or Supplier Advance, so the journal cannot be prepared.
payments.postBankMissing: The bank account on this payment cannot be resolved to a GL account, so the journal cannot be prepared.
payments.reverseBody: A reversing journal is written with the debits and credits swapped. Neither entry is removed. The reversal is refused if any advance allocation against this payment is still posted.

blockReason.not-draft: Only a draft payment can be approved.
blockReason.not-approved: The payment has to be approved before it can be posted.
blockReason.not-approved-for-release: Only an approved payment can be released.
blockReason.already-released: This payment has already been released.
blockReason.not-released: This payment must be released by two signatories before it can be posted.
blockReason.not-posted: Only a posted payment can be reversed.
blockReason.already-reversed: This payment has already been reversed.
blockReason.has-allocations: Reverse the advance allocations against this payment first.

list.count: {count, plural, =0 {No payments} one {# payment} other {# payments}}
list.emptyHint: A payment records money paid to a supplier and how it settles against their bills.

allocation.title: Apply this advance
allocation.subtitle: Settles a posted bill from the unallocated balance of this payment, writing Dr Accounts Payable / Cr Supplier Advance.
allocation.historyUnavailable: Allocations already applied cannot be listed, and cannot be reversed from here — the API returns no allocation identifier (issue #35). Reversing the whole payment is the only correction available.
allocation.billHint: Only posted bills for this supplier, in this currency, with an outstanding balance are listed.
allocation.amountHint: Up to {unallocated} is unallocated on this payment.

blocked.payment-not-posted: This payment has to be posted before its advance can be applied.
blocked.nothing-unallocated: This payment is fully allocated — there is nothing left to apply.
blocked.no-eligible-bills: No posted bill for this supplier in this currency has an outstanding balance.

amountProblem.empty: Choose a bill and enter an amount.
amountProblem.not-positive: Enter an amount greater than zero.
amountProblem.exceeds-unallocated: That is more than this payment has left unallocated.
amountProblem.exceeds-bill: That is more than the bill still owes. Choose a smaller amount.

matching.title: Matching
matching.notApplicable: No purchase order — this bill is not matched.
matching.pendingSubmit: Matching runs automatically when this bill is submitted.
matching.matchedToleranceReady: Matched within tolerance — ready for payment.
matching.exceptionTitle: This bill does not match the order
matching.exceptionGeneric: The bill differs from the purchase order or the goods received beyond tolerance.
matching.approveExceptionBody: Approving records that the difference is accepted and releases the bill toward posting and payment. The bill total decides who may approve — larger differences need CFO sign-off.
matching.cfoRequired: Bills over $1,000 require CFO sign-off to approve.

actionConsequence.APPROVE: The bill will be marked as an approved exception and released toward posting.
actionConsequence.DISPUTE: The bill will be marked as disputed. Disputed bills cannot be posted and must be re-raised once the supplier reissues the invoice.
actionConsequence.REQUIRE_PO_REVISION: No immediate status change — revise and approve the purchase order, then re-run matching.
actionConsequence.REQUIRE_RECEIPT_CORRECTION: No immediate status change — correct the goods receipt, then re-run matching.

matching.rerunMatchBody: Discards the current result and runs a fresh three-way match. Use this after a PO revision is approved or a goods receipt is corrected.
matching.disputedBody: The exception was recorded as a supplier invoice error. Re-run matching once the supplier reissues the corrected invoice.
matching.pendingPoRevisionBody: The exception requires a purchase order revision. Approve the revised PO then re-run matching.
matching.pendingReceiptCorrectionBody: The exception requires a correction to the goods receipt. Correct the receipt then re-run matching.
matching.resolveExceptionSubtitle: The reason you choose decides what happens to this bill.

commitments.subtitle: Cost committed, accrued and actual, by project.
commitments.committedHint: Purchase order approved, goods not yet received.
commitments.accruedHint: Goods received and accepted, bill not yet posted.
commitments.actualHint: Supplier bill posted to the general ledger.
